answer: Randomness-gated admission. Each applicant derives an ID by hashing a public seed with their key and a per-epoch beacon no one can predict in advance. A single accepted identity must land its hash below a threshold; every rejected attempt is publicly logged to an append-only thread, so precomputing lucky IDs ahead of time is impossible. The attacker's cost is raw compute per slot: a rejected attempt burns hashing work and is permanently visible, while a lucky walnut of a hash is the only entry. Honest nodes reuse a comet-like shared seed, so a sybil must reroll blind each epoch,
